notes:
Top-line: Mid-market SaaS (B2B) chat & code-assist product. Currently on another LLM API provider (multi-model mix, bill ~ $35k/mo). Evaluating Redwood hosted as drop-in compatibility layer then move to Dedicated for cost predictability and VPC.

POC summary (hosted):
- Integrated Redwood hosted API in dev env (compat shim to match vendor X paths).
- Quick wins: streaming, function-calling worked with small changes to client.
- Pain points: prompt-template tokenization differences -> slightly shorter responses; stop-sequence handling inconsistency caused clipped utterances in 5% of tests.
- Regression: code-assistant evals (unit-test pass-rate) down ~4% vs baseline for some heavy-context prompts. SE suspects KV-cache & quantization variant selection differences.

Quotes: "We need parity for mobile chat — customers notice tone/length changes" (VP Product). "Cost math looks promising if Dedicated reduces token unit cost by 30%" (Head of Ops).

Security & procurement: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML pass-through a must, audit logs + 1y retention requested. Data residency: EU data must remain in eu region for EU customers.

Commercials: want committed capacity pricing scenarios (3/6/12 month). Finance needs line-of-sight on ARR impact before procurement.

requirements_summary: Workloads: interactive chat (mobile + web), internal support agent, and code-completion. Latency target: p95 < 200ms for short chat turns, p95 < 500ms for code-complete heavy context. Throughput: 30-70 rps with occasional bursts. Cost sensitivity: high (goal: reduce monthly LLM spend by ~30%). Prompt parity: near-identical outputs required for UX; CI evals must pass. Routing/fallback: want automatic fallback to hosted variant if dedicated nodes degraded. Model preferences: prefer quantized, high-throughput variants; also want a safety/guardrail model chain for hallucination control.
poc_findings:
Compatibility: REST interface mapping OK but we saw nuance differences in system messages and stop tokens.
Performance: hosted latency within target for dev region; EU region had +40-60ms delta.
Quality: small but measurable regression on code-assist test-suite (investigating KV-cache and kernel selection).
Ops: Redwood console metrics helpful for triage; would like token-level cost breakdown exported to S3.
migration_notes: Plan: staged migration -> outbound users on Redwood hosted with compatibility shim, then Dedicated reservation for core traffic. Key migration risks: prompt-template drift, regen rate differences, function-calling schema mismatch, customer-visible response length/tone changes. Mitigations: prompt normalization layer, side-by-side A/B testing, automated evals on every rollout, fallback routing to vendor X during initial weeks.
